reviewNote: Teaching points and plans were drafted with AI from standard references (ICDR, ICROP3, ETROP, AAO Preferred Practice Patterns). They are for learning, not patient care, and need sign-off by an ophthalmologist before the module leaves Beta. ROP stage descriptions follow the ROP-VL dataset (CC BY 4.0).

tracks.title: OCT reading

NO: Foveal pit with a smooth, symmetric contour
Every layer continuous, including the ellipsoid zone
No intraretinal or subretinal fluid; RPE line smooth
AMD: Drusen: dome-shaped elevations of the RPE
Neovascular AMD: subretinal fluid, pigment epithelial detachment, subretinal hyperreflective material
Atrophic AMD: RPE loss with light passing into the choroid (hypertransmission)
DME: Hyporeflective cystoid spaces within the retina
Hyperreflective foci and exudates; subretinal fluid in some eyes
ERM: Hyperreflective band on the inner retinal surface
Wrinkled inner retina and a flattened or lost foveal pit
Diffuse thickening; traction cysts in some eyes
RVO: Cystoid macular edema with inner retinal thickening
Branch occlusion: often sectoral, respecting the horizontal raphe
Look for disorganised inner layers and hyperreflective foci
RAO: Acute: thickened, hyperreflective inner retina with shadowing of the outer layers
Chronic: thinning and atrophy of the inner retina
Outer retina and RPE are relatively preserved
VID: Macular hole: full-thickness foveal defect, often with cystic edges
Lamellar hole: partial-thickness defect with an irregular foveal contour
Vitreomacular traction: vitreous still attached at the fovea, distorting it

tracks.pearl: Read an OCT outside in: vitreous and interface, inner retina, fluid spaces, outer retina and ellipsoid zone, RPE, then choroid.

foundation.label: Fluid in the retina (DME or vein occlusion)

plan.AMD: Separate wet from dry: fluid or subretinal material means urgent retina referral for anti-VEGF; drusen alone means monitoring, and AREDS2 supplements for intermediate AMD.
plan.DME: Refer to retina. Anti-VEGF injections are first line for centre-involving DME with reduced vision; optimise glucose, blood pressure and lipids.
plan.ERM: Observe while vision is good. Vitrectomy with membrane peel if distortion or vision loss affects daily life.
plan.RVO: Treat macular edema with anti-VEGF, watch for neovascularisation, and manage systemic risk: blood pressure, diabetes, lipids.
plan.RAO: An acute artery occlusion is an eye stroke: same-day stroke-pathway referral, and check ESR and CRP for giant cell arteritis if over 50.
plan.VID: Full-thickness macular hole: vitrectomy with ILM peel. Lamellar hole or traction: observe, operate if it progresses or vision falls.

tracks.title: Optic disc
tracks.modality: Fundus photograph cropped to the optic disc

normal: Pink neuroretinal rim that follows the ISNT pattern (inferior thickest, then superior, nasal, temporal)
Cup size in proportion to disc size: a large disc can have a large cup
glaucoma: Enlarged vertical cup, or rim thinning that breaks the ISNT pattern
Focal notching, most often inferotemporal or superotemporal
Disc haemorrhage at the rim, bayoneting vessels, beta-zone peripapillary atrophy

tracks.pearl: Judge the rim, not the cup-to-disc ratio alone. Always estimate disc size first.

plan.normal: Routine review. A large cup in a large disc can be normal.
plan.glaucoma: Confirm and stage: IOP, gonioscopy, visual fields and OCT nerve fibre layer. Treat to a target pressure.

tracks.title: Diabetic retinopathy

0: No microaneurysms, haemorrhages, exudates or new vessels
1: Microaneurysms only: tiny, sharp red dots
2: More than microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR
Dot and blot haemorrhages, hard exudates, cotton wool spots
3: 4-2-1 rule, any one of: more than 20 haemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants; venous beading in 2 or more quadrants; prominent IRMA in 1 or more quadrant
4: New vessels on the disc (NVD) or elsewhere (NVE)

tracks.pearl: One macula-centred photograph cannot show all four quadrants, so severe NPDR is a judgement from what is visible. Grade the worst lesion you can see.

plan.1: Rescreen in 12 months; optimise glucose, blood pressure and lipids.
plan.2: Refer to ophthalmology: review in 6 to 12 months without macular oedema, 3 to 6 months with non-central oedema; centre-involving oedema needs treatment (AAO DR PPP 2024).
plan.3: Urgent ophthalmology referral; panretinal laser is often considered, especially if follow-up is uncertain.
plan.4: Urgent treatment: panretinal laser and/or anti-VEGF; vitrectomy for non-clearing vitreous haemorrhage.

tracks.title: Retinopathy of prematurity

normal: No ROP signs; the peripheral retina may still be incompletely vascularised
s1: Demarcation line: a thin, flat white line between vascular and avascular retina
s2: Ridge: the line gains height and width, white to pink
Small isolated neovascular tufts may sit behind it
s3: Extraretinal neovascular proliferation from the ridge into the vitreous
Ragged posterior edge of the ridge
s4: Partial retinal detachment: 4A spares the fovea, 4B involves it
s5: Total retinal detachment (ICROP3: 5A open funnel, 5B closed funnel, 5C with anterior segment changes)
arop: Rapid, severe disease with marked plus disease
Flat, often subtle neovascularisation at the vascular-avascular border, typically posterior
May skip the classic stage sequence
laser: White or pigmented laser spots in the peripheral avascular retina

tracks.pearl: Treat Type 1 ROP (ETROP): zone I any stage with plus, zone I stage 3 without plus, or zone II stage 2 or 3 with plus.

plan.normal: Continue screening until the retina is fully vascularised.
plan.s1: Review in 1 to 2 weeks. Zone and plus disease, not stage alone, decide treatment.
plan.s2: Review in 1 to 2 weeks; treat if it meets Type 1 (zone I with plus, or zone II with plus).
plan.s3: Treat if Type 1 (zone I stage 3, or zone II stage 3 with plus); otherwise review within a week.
plan.s5: Refer for vitreoretinal surgery; visual prognosis is poor.
plan.arop: Treat urgently with laser or anti-VEGF; do not wait for the classic stages.
plan.laser: Follow up for regression and late problems: myopia, strabismus, amblyopia, retinal detachment.
